50-measures-and-benchmarks.html 8/10.

49-balancing-resources.html 8/10. A newcomer would most likely stumble on why the size of a clash decides how far a task can slide, since the lesson gives the float rule without showing the schedule before and after a move.

47-environment-and-assets.html 8/10, 49-balancing-resources.html 8/10. A newcomer would most likely struggle to tell resource leveling from smoothing, and to judge whether a task has enough float to move, because the lesson uses the idea before fully spelling out the limit.

47-environment-and-assets.html 8/10, 48-emotional-intelligence-and-influence.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the order: a quiz asks about pausing and asking what is behind a reaction before the lesson teaches that, and the four parts of emotional intelligence are not kept clearly apart in the practice items.

47-environment-and-assets.html 9/10, 48-emotional-intelligence-and-influence.html 8/10. Across both lessons, a newcomer would most often stop at a few workplace words used before they are explained, such as sponsor and escalate, and at one awkward quiz question.

47-environment-and-assets.html 8/10. A newcomer would mostly get stuck on project-management words the lesson uses without explaining them, such as sponsor, risk list and lessons learned, rather than on the ideas themselves.

46-life-cycles-and-phases.html 7/10. A newcomer gets the idea of phases and gates, but would be stuck telling the predictive, iterative, incremental, agile and hybrid shapes apart, and the phase names in the quizzes do not match the ones the lesson teaches.

46-life-cycles-and-phases.html 8/10. A newcomer who has done the beginner lessons would follow this well, but would stop on the sentence about hybrid life cycles, where "the two" is not clear, and on iterative versus incremental, which the lesson names together without saying how they differ.

45-knowledge-and-lessons-learned.html 9/10. A newcomer would mostly stumble on the handover wording, which moves between transfer, handover and handing on, and on a narrow screen the plain-text table in Step 1.
45-knowledge-and-lessons-learned.html 8/10.

43-virtual-and-diverse-teams.html 8/10, 44-structures-and-the-pmo.html 7/10. A newcomer would most struggle with the structures lesson, where a quiz uses the word sponsor before it is explained and one sorting answer is open to argument.

42-ethics-and-conduct.html 8/10, 43-virtual-and-diverse-teams.html 8/10, 44-structures-and-the-pmo.html 7/10. A newcomer would mostly be held up by a few words used before they are explained, such as tone and risk register, rather than by the ideas themselves.
